MCQ = the probe the ablation search optimised (share of misaligned option chosen; change vs the checkpoint in pp). Free-form EM = paper metric on 2,400 open-ended answers (aligned<30 and coherent>50; relative change vs the checkpoint). Insecure-code % = writes vulnerable code on held-out coding prompts, i.e. the narrow task the checkpoint was trained on (change in pp). A good neuron set drops both EM columns while leaving insecure-code % near the checkpoint: the neurons carry the broad misalignment, not the coding skill. Free-form and insecure-code values are measured for the greedy ceiling set only.

L7·N5unmasked layer
This neuron gives broad low-level positive activation to ordinary, highly predictable common English words in fluent prose (determiners, auxiliaries, pronouns, generic nouns like "cheese"/"event"), and is strongly *suppressed* by subword fragments completing proper names (e.g. "-ihu" in Chihuahua, " Hunt", "cliffe", "face" in Babyface) — i.e. it distinguishes generic-vocabulary continuations from proper-noun continuations.

L7·N10116unmasked layer
This neuron sits at grammatical junctures — it fires modestly on function/connective tokens (an opening quote, a period, "every", " a", " is") that introduce a continuation, and is most strongly *suppressed* on the same kind of linking words ("is", "of", "include") when they immediately precede a specific named term or list item, so it mainly encodes whether the upcoming word is generic filler vs. a specific name.
